title: Automated Inventory Reconciliation Agent
business: Retail logistics firms managing high-volume warehouse stock.
problem: Manual inventory reconciliation is slow, prone to human error, and expensive, often leading to stock discrepancies that delay order fulfillment.
solution: An Agent Runtime implementation that automates the execution loop, handling model turns, tool calls to database APIs, and handoffs to human auditors when discrepancies exceed defined thresholds.
steps: Define an Agent with specific instructions for inventory verification and tools for database lookups.
Configure a RunConfig to manage tool execution concurrency, ensuring database load remains within safe limits.
Initialize the Runner to handle the agent loop, automatically processing model-emitted tool calls.
Implement handoff logic to transition the conversation to a human auditor if the model cannot reconcile a stock count.
Execute the run using Runner.run() to process the full lifecycle from input to final output.
outcome: Reduced manual workload for inventory teams and faster, more accurate stock reconciliation through automated tool-driven verification.
limitation: The runtime loop may hit a MaxTurnsExceeded exception if the agent enters a recursive tool-calling cycle, which can be checked by monitoring for this specific exception type during execution.

diagram.title: Agent Runtime Execution Loop
diagram.description: The flow illustrates how the Runner manages the agent lifecycle, including tool execution and final output generation.

code.content:
from agents import Agent, Runner, RunConfig, ToolExecutionConfig

# Define agent with inventory tools
agent = Agent(name="InventoryAgent", tools=[check_stock, update_db])

# Configure runtime to limit concurrent DB calls
config = RunConfig(tool_execution=ToolExecutionConfig(max_function_tool_concurrency=2))

# Execute the loop
result = await Runner.run(agent, "Reconcile SKU-123", run_config=config)
code.explanation: This code maps to the Automated Inventory Reconciliation Agent by setting up a controlled execution environment that prevents database overloading during automated stock checks.
